summary: Most useful complementary inputs found are CMS’s state/plan-level Exchange Transparency in Coverage Public Use File (PUF) for aggregate claims denials, authorization-related claim denials, resubmissions, and appeals; and the new CMS public prior-authorization reporting requirement for payer-reported approvals, denials, and response times. Neither provides patient-level hospital workflow observations. The CMS PUF is a national/external benchmark at issuer or plan × state × plan-year scope; payer website metrics may offer better payer-level turnaround measures as reporting begins.

sources.title: Health Insurance Exchange Public Use Files (Exchange PUFs)
sources.geography: Exchange issuers/plans in applicable FFE and SBE-FP states; state-level rows, including New Jersey where represented
sources.period: Exchange PUFs span plan years 2014–2026. The PY2026 Transparency in Coverage PUF uses issuer data for PY2024; the examined data dictionary covers claims with 2024 dates of service and receipt/decision during 2024.
sources.grain: Issuer or plan × state × plan year; not facility- or service-specific. Plan-level submissions are required for several fields, while some older periods are aggregated at issuer level.
useful_fields: Claims received and denied, by in-network/out-of-network status
Claims denied due to prior authorization or referral required
observed_facts: CMS describes the PUFs as downloadable and provides a Transparency in Coverage PUF plus a separate data dictionary and disclaimer.

The PY2026 PUF contains PY2024 issuer data. The dictionary describes plan-level claims denied due to prior authorization/referral as non-emergency in-network claims for services requiring prior authorization, referral, approval, or precertification.

Claims and appeals are issuer-reported aggregates and do not identify RWJUH or Saint Peter’s encounters, service-specific policies, actual submission-to-decision intervals, or censored cases. CMS’s disclaimer cautions that aggregate claims and appeals counts do not by themselves indicate issuer quality.
sources.retrieval_next_step: From the CMS Exchange PUF page, download the PY2026 Transparency in Coverage PUF, the matching PY2026 data dictionary, and the applicable disclaimer. Filter the workbook to New Jersey and inspect issuer/plan coverage before using any row. Preserve the original files, retrieval date, sheet/row scope, and the CMS disclaimer; do not infer facility-level values.
limitations: State and plan/issuer aggregation cannot represent either New Brunswick hospital’s workflow directly.
The PUF reports claims and appeals aggregates, not prior-authorization request queue timestamps or actual processing-time distributions.
The PY2026 label refers to the PUF release/plan-year package; the reported data are PY2024.
Applicability depends on New Jersey’s Exchange participation and PUF inclusion; confirm the row exists before treating it as a local payer benchmark.

sources.title: Prior Authorization Metrics Reporting – Overview and Template
sources.geography: Payer-specific public websites for covered payer categories; reporting levels include MA contract, state Medicaid/CHIP FFS, Medicaid managed-care plan, and FFE QHP issuer
sources.period: Metrics reported from the previous calendar year, beginning with 2026 reporting; verify each payer’s posted reporting year and effective policy dates at collection.
sources.grain: Payer/line of business reporting level; required metrics include standard and expedited request approval/denial rates and mean/median elapsed response time, with other recommended or optional breakouts. Not necessarily service × policy version.
useful_fields: Covered medical items/services requiring authorization, with categories, codes, and plain-language descriptions
Standard requests approved and denied; approved after appeal
Mean and median response time from payer receipt to determination
Reporting period and payer line of business
observed_facts: CMS says covered payers must make specified prior-authorization metrics publicly accessible on their websites beginning in 2026, using data from the prior calendar year.
CMS’s template calls for mean and median elapsed time between payer receipt and determination, explicitly distinguishing receipt from provider send time.
CMS recommends reporting both counts and percentages and requires explicit turnaround-time units; the metrics are payer-reported results, distinct from legal or policy deadlines.
sources.retrieval_next_step: For one payer/line of business serving the selected New Brunswick geography, navigate from its public-facing site to its prior-authorization metrics page and save one reporting-year artifact, recording publication date, line of business, denominator/definitions, units, and any service categories. If absent, record a failed public-source lead and next action; do not substitute a deadline for observed processing time.
limitations: This is a reporting template and requirement, not itself a dataset containing local observations.
Reporting begins in 2026; availability and completeness of payer postings must be checked individually.
Metrics may be at payer or contract level rather than plan × service × policy version, and may not identify either hospital.
The examined template page does not establish reuse or redistribution terms for each payer’s posted data.

sources.title: Transparency in Qualified Health Plan Coverage PUF Data Dictionary, PY2026
sources.geography: State-level Exchange issuer and plan records; check for New Jersey rows in the associated PUF
sources.period: Data dictionary specifies PY2024 claims data in the PY2026 PUF; multiple underlying fields have differing history, including plan years 2015–2024 for appeals and PY2018–2024 for some authorization-related claim denials.
sources.grain: Issuer or plan × state × plan year; no hospital or service-specific prior-authorization event grain.
observed_facts: The dictionary identifies issuer-level in-network claims received and denied as state-level aggregates and reports that several apply to plan years 2022–2024.

It defines plan-level claims denied due to prior authorization/referral as non-emergency in-network claims for services requiring prior/pre-authorization, referral, prior approval, or precertification.
It defines internal appeals as requests for review of adverse determinations and internal overturns as final adverse determinations overturned in whole or part.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Use the linked dictionary alongside the PY2026 PUF. Select only New Jersey records and report the exact plan/issuer, sheet, plan year, and populated fields; keep claims denial/resubmission metrics separate from prior-authorization request approval metrics.
limitations: The dictionary describes fields but does not provide the observations; the matching PUF must be downloaded separately.
Claims denied for authorization/referral do not reveal authorization request volume, policy version, or time to decision.
Do not derive denial percentages without verifying denominator compatibility and suppression/missing-value conventions in the actual PUF.

missing_inputs: A verified current policy document for one named payer plan serving New Brunswick, including service-specific prerequisites, decision states, effective dates, and stated standard/expedited deadlines.

Observed authorization request submission, payer receipt, decision, appeal, and resolution timestamps linked to service and policy version; these are not available from the reviewed public aggregates.
A verified matching New Jersey payer public metrics page with actual payer-reported prior-authorization response-time values.
simulation_use: Use New Jersey rows from the CMS Exchange PUF as an explicitly external, payer/plan-level calibration reference for claims denial, resubmission, and appeal stages, subject to confirming row availability and coverage. Use actual CMS-mandated payer website metrics, when found, for payer-reported prior-authorization approval/denial and elapsed-time distributions at their stated reporting grain. Model policy deadlines as separate service/policy-version rules, and represent hospital work queues and censoring only from authorized institutional data or clearly labeled synthetic scenarios; do not infer local delays or probabilities from these sources.
limitations: This is candidate discovery and schema-based evaluation, not dataset acquisition; no PUF or payer file was downloaded or inspected for New Jersey observations.
The four opened primary pages establish CMS PUF scope and field definitions, but do not establish a specific New Jersey payer row or local hospital applicability.
Public inputs do not meet the requested full grain of payer/plan × service × policy version × decision/appeal stage with timestamps.
Rights/access evidence for the PUF is linked to the CMS disclaimer/user agreement; review its terms and the selected file’s attribution requirements before redistribution.
All listed findings require independent verification before use.
